svg.title: Ordering and Hermitian hypotheses prevent two exact failures
svg.desc: The correct Hermitian comparison matches levels by decreasing rank and has largest shift one half within a square root five over four budget. Reversing the second spectrum creates a false slot shift fifteen quarters. Along the real two by two non-Hermitian family whose lower-left entry epsilon is nonnegative, matrix distance from the defective endpoint is epsilon while decreasing-real eigenvalue motion is square root epsilon. Their ratio is unbounded in every relative neighborhood of the endpoint. Epsilon one sixteenth gives the executable instance one quarter versus one sixteenth.
svg.text: Two hypotheses stop two different failures
Ordering fixes the matching; Hermiticity supplies stable real ordered levels.
CONTROL: Hermitian matrices, decreasing order on both sides
equal-rank shifts: 1/2 and 1/4; common Frobenius budget: sqrt(5)/4
The matrix B and its eigenvalue multiset did not change.
It violates the equal-decreasing-rank matching rule.
An unordered multiset does not name corresponding slots.
instance: level motion 1/4 is greater than 1/16
family N_e, e >= 0: motion sqrt(e), distance e
ratio unbounded in every relative neighborhood of J
The project theorem is about decreasing real spectra on intrinsic Hermitian matrices, not arbitrary labelings or general complex matrices.
